Semi-Local Iterative Algorithm

Source: R/centrality-batch67.R
centrality_semi_ia.Rd

The semi-local iterative algorithm (semi-IA; Luan et al. 2021) repeats an update in the manner of eigenvector centrality and HITS, in which a node collects the normalised scores of the nodes within \(r\) steps, weighted by the number of shortest paths to them and divided by the distance: $$X_i(t + 1) = \sum_{j \ne i:\, d_{ij} \le r} \frac{n_{ij}^{\gamma}}{d_{ij}} \frac{X_j(t)}{\|X(t)\|}, \qquad X(0) = 1,$$ with \(d_{ij}\) the distance and \(n_{ij}\) the number of shortest paths. The score is \(X\) at the steady state.

Usage

centrality_semi_ia(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Network input accepted by centrality.

...

Further arguments to centrality. The measure uses semi_ia_radius (default NULL, 3 or 5 by the size of the network), semi_ia_gamma (default 0.2) and semi_ia_max_iter (default 10000).

Value

A named numeric vector with one score per node, in input node order.

Details

The measure is computed on the simple undirected skeleton of the network, so direction, weights, loops and parallel edges are ignored. The source prints its equation (8) with the node's own normalised score \(X'_i\) inside the sum. Read so, the update ranks the nodes by the row sums of the weight matrix and its normalised vector collapses onto one node, which the source's Fig. 7 contradicts. The neighbor's score \(X'_j\) is used, the reading of the eigenvector and HITS updates the source says it follows. The norm is Euclidean, as in the source's HITS normalisation. The steady state is the leading eigenvalue times the unit leading eigenvector of the weight matrix. semi_ia_radius = NULL, the default, takes \(r = 3\) below 1000 nodes and \(r = 5\) from 1000 nodes on, the rule of the source; Inf admits the whole network. semi_ia_gamma is 0.2, the value the source chooses, and must lie in \([0, 1]\). The source stops when two successive normalised vectors differ by less than \(10^{-5}\); here the largest difference must fall below \(10^{-12}\), within at most semi_ia_max_iter updates (default 10000). Past that bound the last iterate is returned with a cograph_no_converge warning; with semi_ia_radius = 1 this happens on a bipartite network, which has no steady state. The source treats connected networks; on a disconnected network, or a one-node network, the measure warns (class cograph_undefined_measure) and returns NA. The source prints no score. It prints the monotonicity of the ranking on the adjective-noun network (0.9997, Table 2), which the implementation reproduces; the value does not separate the two readings of equation (8), so the scores are otherwise checked against the definition only. On four test networks the score ranks nodes closest to icentr (mean Kendall correlation 0.90); with centrality_eigenvector the correlation is 0.69 to 0.84. normalized = TRUE divides the scores by their maximum.

References

Luan, Y., Bao, Z. and Zhang, H. (2021). Identifying influential spreaders in complex networks by considering the impact of the number of shortest paths. Journal of Systems Science and Complexity, 34(6), 2168-2181. doi:10.1007/s11424-021-0111-7 .

See also

centrality_improved_closeness, centrality_eigenvector, centrality_hub, centrality.

Examples

centrality_semi_ia(to_undirected(regulation_net))
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>   2.372646   2.511724   2.611233   2.534338   2.395257   2.410600   2.257798 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>   2.419776   2.504134   2.394968 
centrality_semi_ia(to_undirected(regulation_net), semi_ia_gamma = 0.5)
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>   2.683296   2.836798   2.838076   2.939567   2.792207   2.802541   2.598788 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>   2.801385   2.795802   2.719073
